title: Ant nest in a soil bank: can you tell the worked bank from the landslide?
question: One of these banks has 55 ants tunnelling into it and the other has 55 ants eating into it. Which one looks like something dug a nest in it?
context_md:
**What this is for.** Ants have never been able to tunnel — a gallery in soil closed in 5 frames, so a colony could dig all day and leave only a lower bank. An ant now tamps the wall it cuts into packed soil, which holds itself up, so the tunnel is lined as fast as it is opened.

**The physics is verified and is not what I am asking about.** Same binary both sides, one switch. Enclosed void — empty ground with soil standing over it, which a slumping bank cannot produce — is **130/146/151/133 cells with the tamping and 0/0/0/0 without it**, over four seeds, no overlap. An ASCII dump of the worked bank shows a branching warren of packed-walled galleries; the other is a smooth talus slope with nothing inside it.

**What I am unsure about is whether any of that reaches you.** The galleries are one to two cells wide and packed soil is only soil darkened, so I cannot tell whether a worked bank reads as *worked* or just as a scruffier pile. If the two panes look the same to you, the answer is that the mechanic is invisible and the colour or the gallery size needs to change — that is a more useful result than a correct guess.

Both at frame 8,000, noon held so the light is the same, near face of the bank.

items.label: tamping on — ants line the gallery
items.caption: the shipped behaviour

items.label: tamping off — same ants, no lining
items.caption: ablation: digging unchanged, nothing packs
